turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome to Ashbourne Library. How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Morning! Um, I've just moved to the area, actually, about two weeks ago, and I'd like to join the library, please. I've heard good things.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Lovely, welcome to the town. Dreadful weather this week, isn't it? I hope the removal van didn't get caught in the rain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, it did, we were absolutely soaked, but everything arrived in one piece, which is the main thing. The boxes are still everywhere, though, and I can't find the kettle, which is a proper emergency for a Brit.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I know the feeling, I moved last year and I'm still finding things. Right, let's get you started. It's all brand new for you, so I'll need a few details. Could I take your surname first?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, of course. It's Brammall. That's B-R-A-M-M-A-L-L, two Ms and two Ls.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Brammall, two Ms, two Ls, got it. It's a lovely name, quite unusual round here, I don't think we've got any other Brammalls on the system, and I've worked here nine years. Now, what's your first name?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ha, my dad always said we were the only ones. It's Imogen.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Imogen, lovely, I'll pop that in. Now, you said you've only been here a couple of weeks, so is the address on your paperwork the new one? Which house number are you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, it's the new one, we've only just got the keys sorted. We're at number 318.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Was that 380?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No, 318, the one with the green gate, next to the postbox.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ah, 318, of course. Sorry, I've got a 380 customer who lives on the other side of town, so my ears were primed. Which street is that on?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's Pennycross Lane. That's P-E-N-N-Y-C-R-O-S-S, then Lane. It's the little road behind the allotments, you can't miss it, there's a big oak tree on the corner.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Oh, I know it, very pretty spot. Now, we like to have a contact number in case a reserved book comes in, so do you have a mobile?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I do, but I always forget it, I've only had this phone a month. It's 07700 900 713.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No, 713. Seven-one-three at the end.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: 713, perfect, that's saved. Thank you. And just so we've got a rounded picture, what do you do for a living, if you don't mind me asking?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Not at all. Um, I've just started at a practice on the high street. I'm a dental nurse, mostly helping with fillings and check-ups.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That sounds busy, I bet you see some very nervous faces, and a few grumpy ones too. Anyway, the next thing is where you've come from. Which town or city were you living in before you moved here?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Cheltenham, actually. That's C-H-E-L-T-E-N-H-A-M. I was there for about six years, so it still feels a bit strange, and I keep turning left when I should turn right.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Lovely part of the world, the racecourse and all that, I went once for a hen weekend and never quite recovered. Right, we make the cards here and they're usually ready within a couple of days, and you collect them from the main desk. When would you like to pop back for it?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me think, Tuesday should be fine. Oh, no, I'm working all day Tuesday, sorry. I'll come in on Thursday instead.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thursday it is, I'll put a note on the system. Now, would you like a card just for yourself, or do you have other people at home who'd want to borrow books too?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, yes, there's my husband and our two girls, and they'd all use it. So I'd like the family one, please.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Perfect, that's all sorted, and it's free of charge for residents, and you can renew it online whenever you like. Just one last question for our records. How did you find out about us?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, it was on the council website, when I was reading up on the area.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Brilliant. Thanks, Imogen, that's everything. Enjoy the books, and good luck with the unpacking, I hope you find that kettle soon!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thank you so much, and have a lovely day. Bye!

evidence.quote: Yes, of course. It's Brammall. That's B-R-A-M-M-A-L-L, two Ms and two Ls.
It's Pennycross Lane. That's P-E-N-N-Y-C-R-O-S-S, then Lane.
I'm a dental nurse, mostly helping with fillings and check-ups.
I'll come in on Thursday instead.
So I'd like the family one, please.
Oh, it was on the council website, when I was reading up on the area.
